content:
Apple TV currently boasts a strong lineup of programmes, including standout titles such as Slow Horses, Ted Lasso, Dark Matter, and the new comedy Brothers starring Matthew McConaughey. But there's more good news on the way. Below is a roundup of all Apple TV premieres for October.

The Last First: Winter K2

  • Premiere date: October 2
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Documentary

Directed by Amir Bar-Lev, The Last First: Winter K2 tells a complex, gripping and moving story that examines the extreme mountaineering industry and its ever-changing culture. The film focuses on a 2021 expedition in which Icelandic climber John Snorri Sigurjónsson, along with Pakistani father-and-son duo Ali and Sajid Sadpara, set out to become the first team to summit K2 in winter — the harshest season on the mountain. They soon discover that they are not alone on this perilous climb: they are joined by influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and Nepal's renowned Nims and his team of Sherpas. The Last First: Winter K2 transports viewers to K2's frozen peaks and treacherous weather, revealing an unexpected, layered story of strategy and resolve, class and hierarchy, money and power — all unfolding in life-or-death moments.

The Sisters Grimm Season 2

  • Premiere date: October 2
  • Type: TV Series
  • Category: Kids & Family

Two orphaned sisters navigate a town populated by fairy-tale and fantasy figures, confronting heroes and villains head-on while investigating the mystery of their missing parents. Blending exploration, fantasy and adventure, The Sisters Grimm offers meaningful lessons for viewers of all ages.

Small Prophets

  • Premiere date: October 7
  • Type: TV Series
  • Category: Comedy

Small Prophets is a comedy about the eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley). Since the disappearance of his beloved Clea seven years ago, he has lived an ordinary life — working at a DIY store, regularly visiting his father Brian (Sir Michael Palin), and hoping for Clea's return. One day, Brian shares with him an ancient recipe whose ingredients include rainwater, horse manure, and a dash of alchemy. Armed with the recipe, Michael, with a few doubts, sets out to create Homunculi — magical sprites capable of foretelling the future — hoping they can answer the question burning inside him: "Will I ever see Clea again?"

Matchbox The Movie

  • Premiere date: October 9
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Action

Based on the classic Mattel toy, Matchbox The Movie is a globe-trotting, action-packed adventure about a group of childhood friends whose lives are turned upside down when a CIA undercover agent named Sean (John Cena) — their long-absent former leader — returns to their town, inadvertently dragging them into a wild international chase and tasking them with saving the world.

Tenzing

  • Premiere date: October 16
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Drama

Based on a true story, Tenzing tells a little-known tale: that of the gifted Himalayan climber Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok), who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston), became one of the first to summit Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing gains an ally in expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe). Together they persuade Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) to make Tenzing a full member of the British climbing team rather than a mere supporting figure. In the eyes of Western climbers, Everest is a peak to conquer; for Tenzing, Chomolungma is revered as the sacred goddess of the mountain. The ensuing ascent is fraught with tension born of differing backgrounds, class and competing ambitions, as well as the perils of the mountain itself. Yet, at the top of the world, empire, status and ambition fade away, leaving only two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — and for Tenzing, the realisation of both a lifelong dream and a spiritual calling.

Where's Wanda? Season 2

  • Premiere date: October 21
  • Type: TV Series
  • Category: Dark Comedy

Apple's first German-language series, Where's Wanda?, is a dark comedy about parents Dedo and Carlotta Klatt's desperate search for their missing 17-year-old daughter Wanda, who vanished without a trace months ago. After police investigations turn up nothing, the family decides to take matters into their own hands and, with help from their tech-savvy son Ole, acquire surveillance equipment. Posing as utility company employees, they begin by bugging their next-door neighbours and end up monitoring half the neighbourhood — only to discover that behind every door, none of their neighbours are quite who they pretend to be.

Nocturne

  • Premiere date: October 30
  • Type: TV Series
  • Category: Crime Drama

The series tells the story of Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber), a former soldier turned homicide detective. Weary of the hard streets of Philadelphia, he moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania, hoping for a quiet life. But when the town and his family come under attack by a cunning, demonic serial killer, Jurek Walter (Graham), Jonah must protect everything he holds dear. As his desperate hunt for Jurek's final missing victim forces him to send his surrogate daughter, FBI agent Saga Bauer (Beetz), to confront Jurek head-on, just how far will Jonah go?

New episodes: Slow Horses, Brothers and more

Apple TV will also release new episodes of several currently airing series in October, including:

  • Ted Lasso: Jason Sudeikis-starring comedy, with new episodes through October 7
  • Last Seen: Crime thriller, with new episodes through October 7
  • Slow Horses: Acclaimed British spy drama, with new episodes through October 21
  • Dark Matter: Joel Edgerton-led sci-fi series, with new episodes through October 30
  • Brothers: Comedy co-starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, with new episodes through November 4

Which of Apple TV's October releases are you planning to watch? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, or save with a discounted Apple One bundle.
